title: [Performance][Model] Offload Qwen3.5-VL image preprocessing to NPU
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Qwen3.5-VL image preprocessing (resize, patchify, rescale+normalize) runs on the front-end CPU and saturates the API-server process under multimodal load, slowing down the engine loop.

Add Ascend subclasses of Qwen3.5-VL (dense and MoE) that move the whole pipeline onto the NPU worker: the front-end emits flat raw uint8 plus the original (H, W) and the target grid; the model performs resize (bicubic+antialias, matching HF/PIL), patchify, and normalization (via FusedInputNorm) on the device. The front-end-to-worker payload drops ~8x (uint8, no temporal replication). smart_resize stays on the CPU so placeholder accounting and prompt lengths are unchanged.

Video keeps the CPU patchify path; only rescale+normalize move to the device via the native supports_mm_device_do_normalize mechanism.

Registered through ModelRegistry (architecture overwrite, same pattern as AscendDeepseekV4ForConditionalGeneration in #15457); no vllm or transformers class is monkey-patched.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. On Ascend, Qwen3.5-VL images are preprocessed on the NPU instead of the front-end CPU. No config change required; outputs are numerically equivalent.

### How was this patch tested?

- NPU e2e on Qwen3.5-VL 27B BF16: image-text requests succeed with correct outputs.
- Numerical comparison with stock path: ViT output cosine similarity ~0.999996 (bicubic+antialias reproduces HF/PIL resize).
- Non-Qwen3.5 model regression: qwen2.5-vl routes to the native vllm class, behavior unchanged.
- Front-end CPU utilization significantly reduced under multimodal load.

### How was this patch tested?

accuracy :
GPQA_diamond：85.35
MMMU：81.11

10K input, 300 output with images
performance :
Output token throughput (tok/s)：104 -> 116
TTFT: 2221ms-> 1914ms


- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8cc9aa5ad350f6f80cf3bebb298d410803ff75a9
